question: True or False Question: At least one of response to low-density lipoprotein particle and lymphocyte differentiation is not biological processes commonly involving the gene ITFG2
thinking: ITFG2 is not a well-characterized immune or lipid-response gene and is not commonly annotated to processes like response to LDL particles or lymphocyte differentiation. Therefore at least one (in fact likely both) of those processes do not commonly involve ITFG2.

question: True or False Question: At least one of positive regulation of dopamine metabolic process and DNA packaging is not biological processes commonly involving the gene BAHCC1
thinking: BAHCC1 is a chromatin-associated/BAH-domain protein involved in chromatin organization and DNA packaging; there is no common link to positive regulation of dopamine metabolic processes. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly associated with BAHCC1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of amine biosynthetic process and cerebellar granular layer development is not biological processes commonly involving the gene PROX1
thinking: PROX1 is a developmental homeobox transcription factor involved in organogenesis and neuronal development (e.g. dentate gyrus granule cells, lymphatic endothelial specification) but it is not known to commonly participate in amine biosynthetic processes (biosynthesis of small-molecule amines). Therefore at least one of the two listed processes is not commonly associated with PROX1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of beta-Alanine metabolism - Homo sapiens (human) and The phototransduction cascade is not pathways which commonly contain the gene NMT1
thinking: NMT1 encodes N-myristoyltransferase, involved in protein myristoylation, not core enzymes of beta-alanine metabolism or the phototransduction cascade. Those pathways typically do not include NMT1, so at least one (in fact both) do not commonly contain NMT1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of beta-Alanine metabolism - Homo sapiens (human) and Phosphatidylinositol signaling system - Homo sapiens (human) is not pathways which commonly contain the gene MTMR1
thinking: MTMR1 is a myotubularin phosphatase involved in phosphoinositide (phosphatidylinositol) signaling, not in beta-alanine metabolism. Therefore at least one of the two pathways (beta-alanine metabolism) does not commonly contain MTMR1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Antigen processing: Ubiquitination & Proteasome degradation and beta-Alanine metabolism - Homo sapiens (human) is not pathways which commonly contain the gene KLHL3
thinking: KLHL3 encodes a Cullin3 substrate adaptor involved in ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, so it could appear in ubiquitination/proteasome-related pathway lists. It is not involved in beta‑alanine metabolism, which is a metabolic pathway unrelated to KLHL3 function. Therefore at least one of the two pathways does not commonly contain KLHL3.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Synthesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) and beta-Alanine metabolism - Homo sapiens (human) is not pathways which commonly contain the gene PIGB
thinking: PIGB encodes a mannosyltransferase involved in GPI-anchor biosynthesis, so it is commonly in the GPI synthesis pathway. It is not involved in beta-alanine metabolism, so at least one of the two pathways does not commonly contain PIGB.

question: True or False Question: At least one of EGFR1 and beta-Alanine metabolism - Homo sapiens (human) is not pathways which commonly contain the gene PLSCR1
thinking: PLSCR1 (phospholipid scramblase 1) is a membrane protein involved in phospholipid movement and interferon responses, not an enzyme in amino acid metabolism. It would not be a component of the beta-alanine metabolism pathway, so at least one of the two named pathways does not commonly contain PLSCR1. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PDS5A and SNAP91 is not genes which commonly interact with the gene NECAP1
thinking: True. NECAP1 is an endocytic/clathrin-associated protein and is known to interact with endocytic partners such as SNAP91, whereas PDS5A is a cohesin/regulation-of-chromosome-cohesion protein (nuclear) not known to commonly interact with NECAP1; therefore at least one of the two does not interact with NECAP1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of NOTCH2NLA and PDS5A is not genes which commonly interact with the gene KLK8
thinking: KLK8 (a secreted kallikrein) is known to interact with other proteases, inhibitors and extracellular substrates; NOTCH2NLA (Notch-related) and PDS5A (a cohesin-associated nuclear protein) are not documented common interactors of KLK8. Therefore at least one (in fact both) do not commonly interact with KLK8.

question: True or False Question: At least one of APLF and PDS5A is not genes which commonly interact with the gene IRX5
thinking: APLF (a DNA repair factor) and PDS5A (a cohesin‑associated protein) are not known common interactors of the transcription factor IRX5. It is therefore true that at least one of them (in fact likely both) does not commonly interact with IRX5.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CD1A and PDS5A is not genes which commonly interact with the gene UBTD1
thinking: UBTD1 is associated with ubiquitin-related and cell-cycle/cohesin regulators; CD1A (an antigen-presenting molecule) is unlikely to commonly interact with UBTD1. Even if PDS5A might interact in cohesion contexts, at least one of the two (CD1A) does not commonly interact with UBTD1. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of FASN and ILK is not genes which commonly interact with the gene SF3A1
thinking: SF3A1 is a spliceosome component whose common interactors are other splicing factors (e.g., SF3B proteins, U2 components). FASN (fatty acid synthase) and ILK (integrin-linked kinase) are not typical SF3A1 interactors, so at least one does not commonly interact.

question: True or False Question: At least one of bradykinin receptor binding and oxidoreductase activity is not molecular functions commonly attributed to the gene MPO
thinking: MPO encodes myeloperoxidase, a heme peroxidase with oxidoreductase/peroxidase activity. It is not known to bind bradykinin receptors, so at least one of the two listed functions (bradykinin receptor binding) is not commonly attributed to MPO.

question: True or False Question: At least one of bradykinin receptor binding and GTPase activator activity is not molecular functions commonly attributed to the gene ANKRD27
thinking: ANKRD27 (VARP) is an endosomal trafficking protein that interacts with Rab GTPases and contains a VPS9 domain (a GEF), not a GAP. It is not known to bind bradykinin receptors. Therefore at least one (indeed both) of those listed molecular functions are not commonly attributed to ANKRD27.

question: True or False Question: At least one of bradykinin receptor binding and hydrolase activity, acting on acid anhydrides, in phosphorus-containing anhydrides is not molecular functions commonly attributed to the gene DSCC1
thinking: DSCC1 (DNA replication and sister chromatid cohesion protein 1) is known for roles in DNA replication/repair and cohesion; it is not known as a bradykinin receptor binder nor as an ATPase/hydrolase acting on phosphorus-containing anhydrides. Therefore at least one (indeed both) of those functions are not commonly attributed to DSCC1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of tumor necrosis factor receptor binding and bradykinin receptor binding is not molecular functions commonly attributed to the gene TRAP1
thinking: TRAP1 is an Hsp90-family mitochondrial chaperone with ATP binding and protein-folding activities. It is not known to have bradykinin receptor binding activity (and bradykinin receptor binding is not a common GO molecular function for TRAP1). Therefore at least one of the two listed bindings is not attributed to TRAP1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of oxidoreductase activity, acting on the aldehyde or oxo group of donors, oxygen as acceptor and fatty acid transporter activity is not molecular functions commonly attributed to the gene FABP1
thinking: FABP1 (liver fatty acid–binding protein) is an intracellular fatty acid–binding/transport protein, not an oxidoreductase. The oxidoreductase activity (acting on aldehyde/oxo groups with oxygen as acceptor) is not a function attributed to FABP1, so at least one listed function is not associated with FABP1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of cyclin-dependent protein kinase 5 holoenzyme complex and podosome is not cellular components commonly linked to the gene CDK5R2
thinking: CDK5R2 encodes p39, an activator of CDK5 and is annotated to the cyclin-dependent protein kinase 5 holoenzyme complex. It is not commonly linked to podosomes (specialized adhesion structures), so at least one of the two is not a commonly linked cellular component for CDK5R2.

question: True or False Question: At least one of anchored component of membrane and podosome is not cellular components commonly linked to the gene CD160
thinking: CD160 is a GPI-anchored cell-surface protein and is commonly annotated to membrane/anchored component terms; it is not known to be associated with podosomes (actin-rich adhesion structures). Therefore at least one of the two (podosome) is not commonly linked to CD160.

question: True or False Question: At least one of cell surface and podosome is not cellular components commonly linked to the gene BACE2
thinking: BACE2 is a type I transmembrane aspartyl protease often localized to the plasma membrane and endosomal/secretory compartments (so “cell surface” can be linked), but it is not commonly associated with podosomes. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly linked to BACE2.

question: True or False Question: At least one of perinuclear region of cytoplasm and podosome is not cellular components commonly linked to the gene PRKCE
thinking: PRKCE (PKCε) is commonly annotated to localize to the cytoplasm including the perinuclear region. 'Podosome' is a specialized actin-based structure and is not a commonly reported GO cellular component for PRKCE, so at least one of the two is not linked.

question: True or False Question: At least one of centriole and podosome is not cellular components commonly linked to the gene HSPA6
thinking: HSPA6 (a heat-shock 70 family member) is typically localized to cytosol and nucleus under stress, not to centrioles or podosomes. Thus at least one (in fact both) of those components is not commonly linked to HSPA6.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer Disease, Early Onset and Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia is not diseases commonly associated with the gene HFE
thinking: HFE is the hemochromatosis gene and is linked to iron overload (hereditary hemochromatosis). Early-onset Alzheimer disease and familial Alzheimer disease 3 (with spastic paraparesis/apraxia) are associated with APP/PSEN1/PSEN2, not HFE. Therefore at least one (in fact both) are not commonly associated with HFE.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset and Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia is not diseases commonly associated with the gene NPY
thinking: NPY (neuropeptide Y) is primarily associated with metabolic and neuropsychiatric traits (e.g., obesity, appetite, stress, anxiety, substance use). It is not commonly linked to Alzheimer disease (late-onset) or Familial Alzheimer disease 3, so at least one of the listed diseases is not associated with NPY.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease, Focal Onset and Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia is not diseases commonly associated with the gene NOS3
thinking: NOS3 (endothelial nitric oxide synthase) is primarily linked to vascular and cardiovascular conditions (hypertension, coronary artery disease, preeclampsia, stroke) rather than classical Alzheimer disease genes. Familial Alzheimer disease type 3 is associated with PSEN1, not NOS3. Therefore at least one of the listed conditions is not commonly associated with NOS3.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia is not diseases commonly associated with the gene PCDH11X
thinking: PCDH11X has at best a limited/controversial link to Alzheimer disease; familial Alzheimer disease type 3 (with spastic paraparesis and apraxia) is classically linked to PSEN1 mutations, not PCDH11X. Thus at least one of those conditions is not commonly associated with PCDH11X.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia is not diseases commonly associated with the gene RELN
thinking: RELN (reelin) is classically associated with neuronal migration disorders (e.g., lissencephaly with cerebellar hypoplasia) and has been studied as a modifier in neuropsychiatric diseases, but it is not a common causal gene for Alzheimer disease or for Familial Alzheimer Disease 3 (which is linked to presenilin/other genes). Therefore at least one of the two named Alzheimer conditions is not commonly associated with RELN.

question: True or False Question: At least one of testis and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly over-express the gene CELA1
thinking: CELA1 (chymotrypsin-like elastase 1) is primarily expressed in pancreas and related tissues; testis and lymph node are not typically reported as tissues that commonly over-express CELA1. Therefore at least one (in fact both) do not commonly over-express it.

question: True or False Question: At least one of cerebellum and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly over-express the gene FAM156B
thinking: Likely true. FAM156B is not commonly over-expressed in both tissues; expression atlases do not show strong/consistent over-expression in lymph node (and tissue-specific over-expression in cerebellum is not clearly documented), so at least one of the two is not a common site of over-expression.

question: True or False Question: At least one of medulla oblongata and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly over-express the gene SGPP1
thinking: SGPP1 (sphingosine-1-phosphate phosphatase 1) is not commonly reported as over-expressed in the medulla oblongata; lymphoid tissues (lymph nodes) may show higher expression. Therefore at least one of the two (the medulla oblongata) is not a site that commonly over-expresses SGPP1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of adrenal cortex and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly over-express the gene DECR2
thinking: DECR2 is a metabolic enzyme often expressed in lipid-metabolizing tissues (e.g., adrenal cortex) but not typically high in lymphoid tissue. Therefore at least one of the two (lymph node) is not a common over-expressing site.

question: True or False Question: At least one of cortex of kidney and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly over-express the gene TBC1D13
thinking: It is unlikely that both the kidney cortex and lymph node are listed as tissues that commonly over-express TBC1D13. Public expression resources typically do not report both of these as enriched for TBC1D13, so at least one of them is not a common over-expressing site.

question: True or False Question: At least one of lymph node and brain is not body parts/anatomy which commonly under-express the gene CD55
thinking: CD55 (decay‑accelerating factor) is expressed on many immune tissues including lymph node, so lymph node would not be a common under‑expressor. Therefore at least one of the two is not a body part that commonly under‑expresses CD55.

question: True or False Question: At least one of lymph node and adrenal gland is not body parts/anatomy which commonly under-express the gene LRRN4CL
thinking: LRRN4CL is not broadly under-expressed across all tissues; it has tissue-specific expression (enriched in neural/reproductive tissues) and is not typically reported as commonly under-expressed in the adrenal gland, so at least one of the two (adrenal gland) is not in the set that commonly under-expresses LRRN4CL. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of lymph node and pituitary gland is not body parts/anatomy which commonly under-express the gene PRKCD
thinking: PRKCD (PKCδ) is expressed in immune/lymphoid tissues (e.g., lymph node) rather than being commonly under-expressed there. Therefore at least one of the two (lymph node) is not a tissue that commonly under-expresses PRKCD, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of testis and lymph node is not body parts/anatomy which commonly under-express the gene DRG2
thinking: DRG2 is broadly expressed across tissues and is not commonly listed as under-expressed in both testis and lymph node; therefore at least one of those two is not a tissue that commonly under-expresses DRG2.

question: True or False Question: At least one of lymph node and pituitary gland is not body parts/anatomy which commonly under-express the gene C1QTNF1
thinking: C1QTNF1 (CTRP1) is typically expressed in tissues like adipose and heart; lymph node and pituitary gland are not both commonly listed as tissues that under-express this gene. Therefore at least one of them is not a commonly under-expressing tissue.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Echothiophate and Muromonab is not drugs which commonly belong to the drug class Iodine
thinking: Muromonab (OKT3) is a monoclonal antibody immunosuppressant, not an iodine-class drug. Echothiophate is an organophosphate cholinesterase inhibitor (often used as echothiophate iodide as a salt) and is not typically classified as an "iodine" drug class either. Therefore at least one (indeed muromonab) is not in the iodine drug class.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Epinephrine and Muromonab is not drugs which commonly belong to the drug class Catecholamines
thinking: Epinephrine is a catecholamine, but muromonab (muromonab-CD3, OKT3) is a monoclonal antibody immunosuppressant, not a catecholamine. Therefore at least one is not a catecholamine.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Edetic acid and Muromonab is not drugs which commonly belong to the drug class Calcium Chelating Activity
thinking: Edetic acid (EDTA) is a chelating agent that binds calcium; Muromonab (OKT3) is a monoclonal antibody immunosuppressant, not a calcium chelator. Therefore at least one of them is not in the Calcium Chelating Activity class.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Muromonab and Norelgestromin is not drugs which commonly belong to the drug class Progesterone Congeners
thinking: Muromonab (muromonab‑CD3) is a monoclonal antibody immunosuppressant, not a progestin. Norelgestromin is a synthetic progestin. Therefore at least one of them is not a progesterone congener.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Retapamulin and Muromonab is not drugs which commonly belong to the drug class pleuromutilin
thinking: Retapamulin is a pleuromutilin antibiotic, but muromonab (muromonab-CD3) is a monoclonal antibody (anti-CD3) used for transplant rejection—so it is not a pleuromutilin. Therefore at least one is not in that class.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Muromonab and Haloperidol is not drugs which commonly treat Alzheimer's Disease
thinking: Muromonab (OKT3) is an anti‑CD3 monoclonal antibody used for transplant rejection, not for Alzheimer’s. Haloperidol is an antipsychotic sometimes used to manage agitation/psychosis in dementia. Thus at least one of them is not commonly used to treat Alzheimer’s.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Ziprasidone and Muromonab is not drugs which commonly affect Alzheimer's Disease
thinking: Muromonab (OKT3) is an anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody used to prevent transplant rejection and is not used to treat or commonly affect Alzheimer's disease. Ziprasidone is an antipsychotic sometimes used to manage behavioral symptoms in dementia but is not a common disease-modifying Alzheimer’s drug. Therefore at least one of them (muromonab) is not a drug that commonly affects Alzheimer’s disease.

question: True or False Question: At least one of INS and SEL1L is not genes commonly associated with the disease Alzheimer's Disease, Focal Onset
thinking: INS (insulin) is primarily linked to diabetes and metabolic traits, not commonly to Alzheimer’s Disease; SEL1L is not a commonly recognized Alzheimer’s-associated gene either. Therefore at least one (in fact both) are not commonly associated with Alzheimer’s Disease, Focal Onset.

question: True or False Question: At least one of INS and SEL1L is not genes commonly associated with the disease Alzheimer Disease, Early Onset
thinking: Known causative genes for early-onset Alzheimer disease are APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 (and APOE for risk in late-onset). INS (insulin) and SEL1L are not commonly associated with early-onset Alzheimer disease, so at least one (indeed both) are not associated.

question: True or False Question: At least one of IGF2R and SEL1L is not genes commonly associated with the disease Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset
thinking: Commonly reported genetic risk loci for late-onset Alzheimer disease include APOE, CLU, PICALM, CR1, BIN1, TREM2, ABCA7, SORL1, etc. IGF2R and SEL1L are not generally listed as commonly associated risk genes for late-onset Alzheimer disease, so at least one (in fact both) are not commonly associated.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PSEN1 and PDS5A is not genes commonly associated with the disease Alzheimer Disease, Familial, 3, with Spastic Paraparesis and Apraxia
thinking: PSEN1 (presenilin 1) is a known causative gene for Familial Alzheimer's disease 3 with spastic paraparesis and apraxia. PDS5A is not a gene commonly associated with that disease. Therefore at least one of the two is not associated.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PRNP and PDS5A is not genes commonly associated with the disease Familial Alzheimer-like prion disease
thinking: PRNP (prion protein gene) is a well-known gene associated with familial prion diseases. PDS5A is a cohesin-associated gene not known to be linked to familial Alzheimer-like prion disease. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly associated with that disease.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Pruritus and Dysarthria is not common symptoms of Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD)
thinking: Pruritus (itching) is not a feature of familial Alzheimer disease, and dysarthria (motor speech impairment) is not a typical/common early symptom (language impairment/aphasia is more common). Therefore at least one of them is not common — statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Muscle Hypotonia and Prosopagnosia is not common symptoms of Alzheimer's Disease
thinking: Muscle hypotonia (reduced muscle tone) is not a typical/common feature of Alzheimer’s disease (motor signs occur late or in atypical variants). Prosopagnosia (face-recognition impairment) can occur, especially with posterior cortical involvement or atypical Alzheimer’s variants, but even if it’s uncommon overall, at least one of the two (muscle hypotonia) is not a common symptom—so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of lymph node and dura mater is not common sites of localization of Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD)
thinking: Familial Alzheimer disease is a central nervous system disorder with pathology in brain parenchyma (hippocampus, neocortex, temporal lobes) and cerebral vessels; lymph nodes and dura mater are not common sites of localization (indeed both are uncommon). Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of telencephalon and tendon is not common sites of localization of Alzheimer's Disease
thinking: Alzheimer's disease affects the brain, particularly the telencephalon (cerebral cortex and hippocampus). It does not localize to tendons. Therefore at least one of the two (tendon) is not a common site.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases commonly associated with the disease Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD)
thinking: Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD) is an inherited, typically early‑onset form of Alzheimer’s. While FAD is a form of Alzheimer’s disease generally, it is not commonly associated with Late‑Onset Alzheimer Disease (which is usually sporadic). Therefore at least one of the two listed (Late‑Onset) is not commonly associated with FAD.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD) and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases commonly associated with the disease Alzheimer's Disease
thinking: Both Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD) and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset are recognized forms/variants of Alzheimer’s disease (FAD is familial/early-onset; late-onset is the common sporadic form). Therefore it is false that at least one is not commonly associated with Alzheimer’s disease.

question: True or False Question: At least one of SLC18A2 and PDS5A is not genes which commonly participate in the biological process sequestering of neurotransmitter
thinking: SLC18A2 (VMAT2) is involved in vesicular uptake/sequestration of monoamine neurotransmitters, whereas PDS5A is a cohesin-associated protein involved in chromosome cohesion and not in neurotransmitter sequestration. Thus at least one of them does not participate in that process.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PSMB6 and NR2F6 is not genes which commonly participate in the biological process cell cycle checkpoint
thinking: PSMB6 is a proteasome subunit involved in protein degradation/antigen processing, not a canonical cell‑cycle checkpoint regulator. NR2F6 is an orphan nuclear receptor involved in transcriptional regulation and immune/tumor processes, not a common cell‑cycle checkpoint gene. Therefore at least one (in fact likely both) do not commonly participate in the cell cycle checkpoint.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PDS5A and NOX3 is not genes which commonly participate in the biological process response to gravity
thinking: PDS5A is a cohesin-associated protein involved in chromosome cohesion and cell cycle processes, not known to function in gravity sensing. NOX3 is an NADPH oxidase expressed in the inner ear and implicated in vestibular/gravity response. Therefore at least one of the two (PDS5A) does not commonly participate in response to gravity.

question: True or False Question: At least one of RPL10L and DNAJC10 is not genes which commonly participate in the biological process ribosomal large subunit assembly
thinking: RPL10L is a ribosomal protein-like gene (likely involved in large subunit function), but DNAJC10 (ERdj5) is an ER-resident chaperone involved in protein folding/ERAD, not ribosomal large subunit assembly. Thus at least one does not commonly participate.

question: True or False Question: At least one of NEFL and PDS5A is not genes which commonly participate in the biological process regulation of axon diameter
thinking: NEFL (neurofilament light chain) is well-known to influence axon caliber, whereas PDS5A is a cohesin-associated protein involved in chromosome cohesion and not known to participate in regulation of axon diameter. Thus at least one (PDS5A) does not commonly participate in that process.

question: True or False Question: At least one of BBC3 and DNAJC10 is not genes common in the pathway DNA Damage Response
thinking: BBC3 (PUMA) is a p53-responsive pro-apoptotic gene often implicated in DNA damage–induced apoptosis and is commonly associated with the DNA damage response. DNAJC10 (ERdj5) is an ER protein disulfide isomerase involved in ER stress/protein folding, not a common DNA damage response gene. Therefore at least one of the two is not common in the DNA Damage Response pathway.

question: True or False Question: At least one of HAGH and PDS5A is not genes common in the pathway methylglyoxal degradation I
thinking: HAGH (hydroxyacylglutathione hydrolase, glyoxalase II) is part of methylglyoxal/glyoxalase pathways, while PDS5A is a cohesion-associated protein unrelated to methylglyoxal degradation. Therefore at least one (PDS5A) is not a common gene in that pathway.

question: True or False Question: At least one of ACSM1 and PDS5A is not genes common in the pathway Phenylacetate Metabolism
thinking: PDS5A is a cohesin/regulatory protein involved in chromosome cohesion, not a metabolic enzyme in Phenylacetate Metabolism. Even if ACSM1 (an acyl‑CoA synthetase) could be linked to acylation of phenylacetate, PDS5A is not, so at least one is not common in that pathway.

question: True or False Question: At least one of HPRT1 and PDS5A is not genes common in the pathway guanine and guanosine salvage
thinking: HPRT1 (hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase) is a core enzyme in guanine/guanosine salvage. PDS5A is a cohesin-associated protein unrelated to purine salvage, so at least one (PDS5A) is not a gene common to that pathway.

question: True or False Question: At least one of SEL1L and ANAPC7 is not genes common in the pathway Regulation of APC/C activators between G1/S and early anaphase
thinking: ANAPC7 is a known APC/C subunit and is part of APC/C-related pathways. SEL1L is an ER-associated degradation protein and not a known member of the 'Regulation of APC/C activators between G1/S and early anaphase' pathway. Therefore at least one of the two is not in that pathway.

question: True or False Question: At least one of ZDHHC1 and SEL1L is not genes which commonly perform the molecular function S-acyltransferase activity
thinking: ZDHHC1 is a member of the DHHC family of protein S-acyltransferases, while SEL1L is an ERAD adaptor protein and is not known to have S-acyltransferase activity. Thus at least one of them (SEL1L) does not perform S-acyltransferase activity.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CNBD2 and MAT2B is not genes which commonly perform the molecular function cAMP binding

thinking: U1 snRNA binding is a specific function of core U1 snRNP proteins (e.g. SNRNP70, SNRPA, SNRPC). question: True or False Question: At least one of APOE and PDS5A is not genes commonly associated with the cellular component intermediate-density lipoprotein particle
thinking: APOE encodes apolipoprotein E, which is a component of lipoprotein particles (including IDL). PDS5A is a cohesin-associated protein involved in chromosomal cohesion and is not associated with lipoprotein particles. question: True or False Question: At least one of PDS5A and TDRD5 is not genes commonly associated with the cellular component chromatoid body
thinking: TDRD5 is a Tudor-domain protein known to localize to the chromatoid body in male germ cells, whereas PDS5A is a cohesin regulatory protein involved in chromosome cohesion and not associated with the chromatoid body. question: True or False Question: At least one of EXOSC6 and DNAJC10 is not genes commonly associated with the cellular component exosome (RNase complex)
thinking: EXOSC6 is a known core subunit of the RNA exosome complex. DNAJC10 (an ER-localized DnaJ family protein/disulfide isomerase) is not associated with the RNA exosome. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly associated with the exosome.

question: True or False Question: At least one of MS4A2 and PDS5A is not genes commonly associated with the cellular component Fc-epsilon receptor I complex
thinking: MS4A2 (FCER1B) encodes the beta chain of the high-affinity IgE receptor (FcεRI) and is associated with the Fc-epsilon receptor I complex. PDS5A is a cohesion-related protein involved in sister chromatid cohesion and is not associated with the FcεRI complex. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly associated with that complex.

question: True or False Question: At least one of FASN and VEGFA is not genes commonly associated with the cellular component secretory granule lumen
thinking: FASN (fatty acid synthase) is a cytosolic/ER-associated enzyme and is not a secreted protein or commonly annotated to the secretory granule lumen. VEGFA is secreted and can be associated with secretory pathways, but because FASN is not, the statement that at least one of them is not associated with the secretory granule lumen is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of LDHB and SEL1L is not genes which are commonly over-expressed in cardiac ventricle
thinking: LDHB is highly expressed in heart/ventricle tissue, but SEL1L is a more ubiquitously expressed ERAD-related gene and is not typically listed as commonly over-expressed in cardiac ventricle. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly over-expressed there.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PDS5B and G3BP2 is not genes which are commonly over-expressed in smooth muscle tissue
thinking: Neither PDS5B nor G3BP2 are known as genes commonly over-expressed specifically in smooth muscle tissue; therefore it is very likely that at least one of them is not commonly over-expressed there.

question: True or False Question: At least one of MAT2B and AFTPH is not genes which are commonly over-expressed in saliva-secreting gland
thinking: MAT2B (methionine adenosyltransferase 2B) and AFTPH (aftiphilin) are not known canonical salivary-gland–specific / commonly over‑expressed secretory genes (salivary glands typically overexpress amylases, mucins, proline‑rich proteins, BPIFA2, etc.). Therefore at least one (in fact likely both) is not commonly over‑expressed in saliva‑secreting glands.

question: True or False Question: At least one of IFI27L2 and MAT2B is not genes which are commonly over-expressed in spinal cord
thinking: There is no evidence that both IFI27L2 and MAT2B are commonly over-expressed in spinal cord tissue. IFI27L2 is an interferon-inducible gene often linked to immune responses, and MAT2B is a broadly expressed metabolic enzyme; it is unlikely that both are commonly over-expressed in spinal cord, so at least one is not.

question: True or False Question: At least one of DNAJC10 and PHETA2 is not genes which are commonly over-expressed in uterine cervix
thinking: There is no strong evidence that both DNAJC10 and PHETA2 are commonly over-expressed in the uterine cervix; at least one (and likely both) are not commonly over-expressed in that tissue, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of VPS25 and SEL1L is not genes which are commonly under-expressed in cardiac ventricle
thinking: True. There is no strong evidence that both VPS25 and SEL1L are commonly under-expressed in cardiac ventricle; these genes are broadly expressed (SEL1L is involved in ER-associated degradation and expressed in heart), so at least one is not under-expressed.

question: True or False Question: At least one of HSD11B2 and MAT2B is not genes which are commonly under-expressed in smooth muscle tissue
thinking: These two genes are not both known as commonly downregulated in smooth muscle. MAT2B is broadly expressed (not typically under-expressed in smooth muscle), and HSD11B2 is tissue-specific rather than classically listed as commonly under-expressed in smooth muscle. Therefore at least one is not commonly under-expressed.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CAD and SLC23A2 is not genes which are commonly under-expressed in saliva-secreting gland
thinking: CAD is a broadly expressed housekeeping gene involved in pyrimidine synthesis and is unlikely to be commonly under-expressed in saliva-secreting glands. Even if SLC23A2 expression varies, it is unlikely both genes are commonly under-expressed there, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of DGAT2 and MAT2B is not genes which are commonly under-expressed in spinal cord
thinking: There is no strong evidence that both DGAT2 and MAT2B are commonly under-expressed in spinal cord tissue. At least one (likely both) are not reported as commonly under-expressed there, so the statement that at least one is not commonly under-expressed is true.

thinking: These two genes are not recognized as commonly downregulated in uterine cervix. Therefore at least one (indeed likely both) is not commonly under-expressed.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly localize to choroid plexus
thinking: Alzheimer’s disease (including late-onset Alzheimer’s) is a neurodegenerative disorder affecting cortex, hippocampus and related brain regions, not a condition that commonly localizes to the choroid plexus. question: True or False Question: At least one of Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD) and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly localize to lymphoid tissue
thinking: Both Familial Alzheimer Disease and Late-Onset Alzheimer Disease are neurodegenerative disorders of the central nervous system (brain) characterized by amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, not diseases that commonly localize to lymphoid tissue. Therefore at least one (in fact both) do not localize to lymphoid tissue.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly localize to neuropil
thinking: Both terms refer to the same condition (Alzheimer disease, including late-onset). Alzheimer pathology typically involves the neuropil (extracellular amyloid/neuritic plaques and neuropil threads), so both are diseases that commonly localize to neuropil. Therefore the statement is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly localize to blood vessel
thinking: Alzheimer’s disease (including late-onset AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder of brain parenchyma with plaques/tangles, not primarily a disease that commonly localizes to blood vessels (though cerebral amyloid angiopathy can involve vessels). Thus at least one (in fact both) do not commonly localize to blood vessels.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly localize to cerebellar nuclear complex
thinking: Alzheimer disease (including late-onset) primarily involves cerebral cortex and hippocampus rather than the cerebellar nuclei. They are not commonly localized to the cerebellar nuclear complex, so at least one (in fact both) are not.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Familial Alzheimer Disease (FAD) and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly present the symptom Ataxia
thinking: Alzheimer disease (both familial/early-onset forms and late-onset forms) primarily present with cognitive decline and memory impairment; cerebellar signs/ataxia are not common presenting features. Therefore at least one (indeed both) do not commonly present ataxia.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly present the symptom Sleep Disorders, Circadian Rhythm
thinking: Both Alzheimer’s disease (including the usual late‑onset form) frequently cause sleep–wake and circadian rhythm disturbances (e.g., sundowning, fragmented sleep, SCN pathology). Therefore it is not true that at least one of them does not commonly present circadian rhythm sleep disorders.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly present the symptom Urinary Incontinence, Urge
thinking: Urge urinary incontinence (particularly in later stages) is a common feature of Alzheimer disease, including the typical late-onset form, so both conditions commonly present this symptom. Therefore the claim that at least one does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly present the symptom Paraparesis, Spastic
thinking: Alzheimer disease (including late-onset) primarily causes cognitive decline and memory loss; spastic paraparesis is not a common presenting feature of Alzheimer’s. Therefore at least one (in fact both) of the listed conditions do not commonly present with spastic paraparesis.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer Disease, Late Onset is not diseases which commonly present the symptom Aphasia, Broca
thinking: Broca (expressive) aphasia is most often due to focal lesions (e.g., stroke). Typical Alzheimer disease, including late‑onset AD, more commonly causes progressive word‑finding, anomia, or logopenic PPA patterns rather than classic Broca’s aphasia. Therefore at least one (in fact both) do not commonly present Broca aphasia.

question: True or False Question: At least one of ADRB2 and KCNH2 is not genes which commonly bind to the drug Sotalol
thinking: Sotalol is a nonselective beta-blocker (binds beta receptors including ADRB2) and also blocks the hERG potassium channel encoded by KCNH2. Therefore both genes commonly bind sotalol, so the claim that at least one does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CYP2B6 and CYP2C9 is not genes which commonly bind to the drug Diclofenac
thinking: Diclofenac is primarily metabolized by CYP2C9 (with contributions from CYP3A4); CYP2B6 is not commonly involved in diclofenac binding/metabolism. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly binding diclofenac.

question: True or False Question: At least one of ABCC2 and ABCG2 is not genes which commonly bind to the drug Irinotecan
thinking: Both ABCC2 (MRP2) and ABCG2 (BCRP) are ABC transporters known to transport/efflux irinotecan and its active metabolite SN-38 (and metabolites like SN-38G). Therefore it is not true that at least one of them does not commonly interact with irinotecan.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 is not genes which commonly bind to the drug Cevimeline
thinking: Both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 are reported hepatic enzymes involved in the metabolism (binding) of cevimeline, so it is false that at least one of them is not commonly involved.

question: True or False Question: At least one of SCN2A and SCN9A is not genes which commonly bind to the drug Lamotrigine
thinking: Lamotrigine is an anticonvulsant that acts primarily on CNS voltage-gated sodium channels such as Nav1.1/1.2 (SCN1A, SCN2A). It is not typically described as commonly targeting the peripheral pain channel Nav1.7 (SCN9A). Therefore at least one of the two (SCN9A) is not a common lamotrigine target.

question: True or False Question: At least one of HOXC6 and RRS1 is not genes commonly subject to increased expression by the drug Conjugated estrogens
thinking: HOXC6 is known to be estrogen-responsive and can be upregulated by estrogens, while RRS1 (a ribosome biogenesis regulator) is not commonly reported as being induced by conjugated estrogens. Therefore at least one of the two is not commonly increased by that drug.

question: True or False Question: At least one of SOCS2 and PIK3CA is not genes commonly subject to increased expression by the drug Quinethazone
thinking: Quinethazone (a thiazide-like diuretic) is not known to commonly upregulate both SOCS2 and PIK3CA. It is unlikely that both genes are commonly increased by this drug, so at least one is not commonly subject to increased expression.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PNP and FHL2 is not genes commonly subject to increased expression by the drug Clofarabine
thinking: I found no evidence that both PNP and FHL2 are commonly upregulated by clofarabine; while nucleoside metabolism genes might be affected, FHL2 is not a commonly reported gene induced by clofarabine, so at least one of the two is not commonly increased. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of JMJD6 and CDH3 is not genes commonly subject to increased expression by the drug Colchicine
thinking: Colchicine primarily affects microtubules and inflammatory pathways; there is no evidence that it commonly upregulates both JMJD6 and CDH3. At least one (and likely both) are not commonly increased by colchicine, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of CNPY3 and SFTPA2 is not genes commonly subject to increased expression by the drug Flurbiprofen
thinking: There is no evidence that flurbiprofen commonly upregulates CNPY3 or SFTPA2; these are not known common transcriptional targets of this NSAID, so it is very unlikely both are commonly increased. Therefore at least one is not commonly increased.

question: True or False Question: At least one of DNAJA3 and ALAS1 is not genes commonly subject to decreased expression by the drug Quinidine
thinking: There is no strong evidence that both DNAJA3 and ALAS1 are commonly downregulated by quinidine. It is unlikely that quinidine commonly decreases expression of both genes, so at least one is not commonly subject to decreased expression.

question: True or False Question: At least one of EBNA1BP2 and TXNDC9 is not genes commonly subject to decreased expression by the drug Quetiapine
thinking: I am not aware of evidence that quetiapine commonly causes decreased expression of both EBNA1BP2 and TXNDC9. These genes are not typical, well-documented targets of quetiapine-induced downregulation, so it is very likely that at least one of them is not commonly decreased by the drug.

question: True or False Question: At least one of SLC25A4 and CLTB is not genes commonly subject to decreased expression by the drug Chlormezanone
thinking: I am not aware of evidence that chlormezanone commonly decreases expression of both SLC25A4 and CLTB. It's unlikely both are commonly downregulated by this drug, so at least one is not — statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of LBR and CDC45 is not genes commonly subject to decreased expression by the drug Bromocriptine
thinking: There is no strong evidence that bromocriptine commonly causes decreased expression of both LBR and CDC45. It’s unlikely that both genes are consistently downregulated by bromocriptine, so at least one is not commonly decreased.

question: True or False Question: At least one of PEG10 and MBOAT7 is not genes commonly subject to decreased expression by the drug Flunarizine
thinking: There is no strong evidence that flunarizine commonly causes decreased expression of both PEG10 and MBOAT7; it is unlikely both are regularly downregulated by this drug, so at least one is not commonly decreased.

question: True or False Question: At least one of DNA Polymerase Inhibitors and Nucleoside Analog is not classes which commonly include the drug Valaciclovir
thinking: False. Valaciclovir (valacyclovir) is a prodrug of acyclovir, a guanosine nucleoside analog that inhibits viral DNA polymerase, so it is commonly classified as both a nucleoside analog and a DNA polymerase inhibitor.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Decreased Platelet Aggregation and P2Y12 Receptor Antagonists is not classes which commonly include the drug Clopidogrel
thinking: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet agent that works as a P2Y12 receptor antagonist and produces decreased platelet aggregation. Therefore both listed classes commonly include clopidogrel, so the claim that at least one does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone Receptor Antagonists and Decreased GnRH Secretion is not classes which commonly include the drug Cetrorelix
thinking: Cetrorelix is a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) receptor antagonist, so it belongs to that class. It does not act by decreasing GnRH secretion itself (it blocks the receptor), so the “Decreased GnRH Secretion” class would not commonly include cetrorelix. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Vitamin K and Reversed Anticoagulation Activity is not classes which commonly include the drug Phylloquinone
thinking: Phylloquinone is vitamin K1 (so it belongs to the Vitamin K class) and is used clinically to reverse anticoagulation (e.g., warfarin reversal). Therefore both named classes commonly include phylloquinone, so the statement claiming at least one does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Histamine H1 Receptor Antagonists and Decreased Histamine Release is not classes which commonly include the drug Epinastine
thinking: Epinastine is an H1-receptor antagonist and also inhibits histamine release from mast cells (mast cell stabilizer). Therefore both listed classes commonly include epinastine, so the statement that at least one is not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Bosutinib and Crizotinib is not drugs which commonly bind to the gene FGR
thinking: Crizotinib is an ALK/ROS1/MET inhibitor and is not commonly reported to bind the Src-family kinase FGR. Bosutinib is a Src/ABL inhibitor and may inhibit Src-family kinases (potentially including FGR), so at least one of the two (crizotinib) does not commonly bind FGR. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Ruxolitinib and Sunitinib is not drugs which commonly bind to the gene MAST1
thinking: Ruxolitinib is a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor and Sunitinib targets VEGFR, PDGFR, c-KIT, FLT3, RET, etc. Neither is commonly reported to bind MAST1, so at least one (in fact both) do not commonly bind MAST1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Ponatinib and Crizotinib is not drugs which commonly bind to the gene FLT3
thinking: Ponatinib is a multi-kinase inhibitor that commonly inhibits FLT3 (among others). Crizotinib primarily targets ALK, ROS1 and MET and is not commonly a FLT3 inhibitor. Therefore at least one of them (crizotinib) does not commonly bind FLT3.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Tamoxifen and Estrone sulfate is not drugs which commonly bind to the gene ESR2
thinking: Tamoxifen is a SERM that binds both ERα (ESR1) and ERβ (ESR2). Estrone sulfate is a circulating estrogen conjugate/prohormone with very low direct affinity for estrogen receptors and is mainly converted to estrone/estradiol; it is not commonly described as directly binding ESR2. Therefore at least one of them does not commonly bind ESR2.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Bromodiphenhydramine and Cefradine is not drugs which commonly bind to the gene SLC22A6
thinking: SLC22A6 encodes OAT1, which commonly transports organic anions including many beta‑lactam antibiotics (some cephalosporins). Cefradine (a first‑generation cephalosporin) may interact with OATs, but bromodiphenhydramine (a diphenhydramine derivative/antihistamine) is not a typical OAT1 substrate. Therefore at least one of the two does not commonly bind SLC22A6.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Estriol and Estradiol is not drugs which commonly increase expression of the gene SLC25A46
thinking: There is no evidence that both estriol and estradiol are commonly reported to increase SLC25A46 expression; it is unlikely that both do, so at least one does not. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Methotrexate and Mycophenolate mofetil is not drugs which commonly increase expression of the gene SPAG7
thinking: There is no common evidence that methotrexate or mycophenolate mofetil commonly upregulate SPAG7; it is very unlikely both do, so at least one does not. Therefore the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Digitoxin and Niclosamide is not drugs which commonly increase expression of the gene KDM6B
thinking: There is no strong evidence that both digitoxin and niclosamide commonly increase expression of KDM6B (JMJD3). At least one (and likely both) do not commonly upregulate KDM6B, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Bisacodyl and Digoxin is not drugs which commonly increase expression of the gene KHDC4
thinking: There is no evidence that bisacodyl or digoxin are commonly reported to increase expression of KHDC4; therefore it is almost certain that at least one of them does not increase KHDC4 expression (in fact likely neither does).

question: True or False Question: At least one of Digoxin and Everolimus is not drugs which commonly increase expression of the gene KBTBD2
thinking: There is no evidence that both digoxin and everolimus are commonly reported to increase expression of KBTBD2. For the statement to be false, both drugs would have to commonly upregulate KBTBD2, which is not supported by literature or gene‑expression databases, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Fluspirilene and Imatinib is not drugs which commonly decrease expression of the gene DECR1
thinking: Neither fluspirilene (a typical antipsychotic acting on dopamine receptors) nor imatinib (a BCR-ABL/c-Kit/PDGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor) are known to commonly downregulate DECR1 expression in the literature or typical drug–gene interaction databases. Therefore at least one (in fact both) do not commonly decrease DECR1 expression.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Podofilox and Vinblastine is not drugs which commonly decrease expression of the gene COQ8A
thinking: There is no evidence that either podofilox or vinblastine are commonly reported to decrease expression of COQ8A (ADCK3). It is therefore safe to say that at least one of them (in fact likely both) does not commonly decrease COQ8A expression.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Irinotecan and Gemcitabine is not drugs which commonly decrease expression of the gene RMND1
thinking: There is no common evidence that both irinotecan and gemcitabine decrease expression of RMND1. At least one (and likely both) are not known to commonly downregulate RMND1, so the claim that at least one is not such a drug is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Dactinomycin and Bortezomib is not drugs which commonly decrease expression of the gene MRPL58
thinking: Dactinomycin (actinomycin D) is a general transcription inhibitor and could reduce many mRNAs including nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins, but bortezomib is a proteasome inhibitor and is not commonly reported to specifically decrease MRPL58 expression. It is therefore unlikely that both drugs commonly decrease MRPL58, so the statement is true.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Afatinib and Dabrafenib is not drugs which commonly decrease expression of the gene DKC1
thinking: Afatinib (an EGFR/ErbB inhibitor) and Dabrafenib (a BRAF inhibitor) are targeted kinase inhibitors and are not known as drugs that commonly decrease expression of DKC1. It is therefore correct that at least one of them is not a drug that commonly downregulates DKC1 (in practice neither is commonly reported to do so).

question: True or False Question: At least one of negative regulation of protein import into nucleus and growth is not biological processes commonly involving the gene MTOR
thinking: MTOR (mTOR) is a central regulator of cellular growth and also negatively regulates nuclear import of certain proteins (e.g., phosphorylation of TFEB retains it in the cytosol). Thus both listed processes commonly involve MTOR, so the claim that at least one does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of spinal cord development and pattern specification process is not biological processes commonly involving the gene DBX1
thinking: DBX1 (developing brain homeobox 1) is a transcription factor known to function in spinal cord development and in pattern specification processes (it helps specify neuronal progenitor domains). Both processes commonly involve DBX1, so the claim that at least one of them does not is false.

question: True or False Question: At least one of regulation of synapse organization and regulation of neurogenesis is not biological processes commonly involving the gene PDLIM5
thinking: PDLIM5 is a PDZ-LIM scaffolding protein linked to cytoskeleton and postsynaptic organization and is commonly associated with synapse-related processes, but it is not commonly annotated as a regulator of neurogenesis. Therefore at least one of the two processes (regulation of neurogenesis) is not commonly involving PDLIM5.

question: True or False Question: At least one of negative regulation of oxidoreductase activity and regulation of oxidoreductase activity is not biological processes commonly involving the gene DAOA
thinking: DAOA (G72) is known to modulate D-amino-acid oxidase (an oxidoreductase), i.e. it is involved in regulation (typically activation) of oxidoreductase activity. It is not commonly described as mediating negative regulation of oxidoreductase activity. Thus at least one of the two GO terms (negative regulation) does not commonly involve DAOA.

question: True or False Question: At least one of nucleic acid transport and cellular response to lipopolysaccharide is not biological processes commonly involving the gene UPF1
thinking: UPF1 is primarily involved in mRNA surveillance, nonsense-mediated decay, RNA processing and related nucleic acid (mRNA) metabolism. It is not commonly associated with the cellular response to lipopolysaccharide (an innate immune/bacterial endotoxin response). Therefore at least one of the two processes (cellular response to LPS) is not commonly involving UPF1.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Pathways in cancer - Homo sapiens (human) and GPCR downstream signaling is not pathways which commonly contain the gene LPAR6
thinking: LPAR6 encodes a lysophosphatidic acid receptor (a GPCR), so it is part of GPCR downstream signaling. It is not typically listed as a common component of the broad 'Pathways in cancer' map, so at least one of the two pathways does not commonly contain LPAR6.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Major pathway of rRNA processing in the nucleolus and cytosol and Formation of a pool of free 40S subunits is not pathways which commonly contain the gene RPL36AL
thinking: RPL36AL encodes a 60S (large subunit) ribosomal protein involved in rRNA processing/60S assembly, so it is expected in the major rRNA processing pathway but not in formation of free 40S (small subunit) pools. Therefore at least one of the two listed pathways does not commonly contain RPL36AL.

question: True or False Question: At least one of Neuronal System and Potassium Channels is not pathways which commonly contain the gene KCNH6
thinking: KCNH6 encodes a voltage-gated potassium channel and is commonly included in potassium channel pathway annotations, but it is not typically listed specifically in the broad “Neuronal System” pathway in common pathway databases. Thus at least one of the two pathways does not commonly contain KCNH6.

question: True or False Question: At least one of TP53 regulates transcription of additional cell cycle genes whose exact role in the p53 pathway remain uncertain and Gene Expression is not pathways which commonly contain the gene CNOT2
thinking: The first clause is essentially true: TP53 (p53) is a transcription factor that regulates many cell-cycle genes, including some whose precise roles in the p53 pathway remain unclear. The second clause is false: CNOT2 (part of the CCR4–NOT complex) is commonly associated with gene expression/transcription-related pathways, so “Gene Expression is not [a] pathway which commonly contain[s] CNOT2” is incorrect.
